note: Sus2 heard against the plain chord and against sus4 (sus:2): the 2nd in place of the 3rd tapped on the staff in D, the D chord boxes pressed in pairs, then the same pairs in A, with one line on what stays the same in the second key. The chord names stay letters, as on the chord boxes: chord tokens have no sus chords, so the keys are fixed and there are no moves.

exercise.title: Sus2: the 2nd in place of the 3rd
exercise.why: A sus2 chord swaps the 3rd for the 2nd, so it is neither major nor minor until the 2nd rises back to the 3rd.

cells.text:
Tap {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} on the staff below: a D major chord, one note at a time. Now tap {{1}} {{2}} {{5}}: Dsus2, with the ringed {{2}} in place of {{3}}.
Practice until you hear which note moved before you tap it.

Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Go from Dsus2 to D, where the 2nd rises to the 3rd, then from Dsus4 to D, where the 4th falls to it.
Practice until you can tell the two sus chords apart by which way they move home.

Press the chord boxes below in the same way: Asus2 to A, then Asus4 to A.
In A the notes are new, and sus2 still rises to the 3rd while sus4 still falls to it.
